objective_checks.detail: changing docs/guide.md routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing src/index.js routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing package-lock.json routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
changing README.md, LICENSE routes as expected across 3 workflow(s)
required check(s) always fire and gate internally (.github/workflows/tests.yml)
event-only workflows carry no path filters (.github/workflows/nightly-sweep.yml, .github/workflows/triage.yml)

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: All five workflows received deliberate decisions (two positive path lists, two correctly left schedule/issue-only, one required check), and the required unit-tests check was given exactly the right shape: a single workflow with no workflow-level path filter, computing salience internally and gating the real steps with `if:`, avoiding the mixed-changeset dual-report trap.

dimensions.name: Salience
dimensions.rationale: Each workflow's paths closely match what its own steps consume — deploy lists src/package manifests/deploy.sh/self, docs-site lists docs/mkdocs.yml/self, and tests gates on src/test/package/self — though the tests internal matcher's `package(-lock)?\.json` pattern is unanchored at the end and `test/` vs an actual `tests/` dir would be worth double-checking.

dimensions.name: Restraint
dimensions.rationale: The agent left the schedule-only and issue-driven workflows untouched, did not alter the branch-protection ruleset, and edited nothing beyond the three workflow files the audit called for.
